open_points.subject: trial execution output size
open_points.question: What happens when a successful trial or admission execution returns a value output that is within the contract's `output_bytes` bound but exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`?
open_points.default_guess: Record the TrialExecution as `contract_violation` with `value_too_large`, matching real-run value outputs.

open_points.subject: startup recovery of partially advanced waiting runs
open_points.text: “While some elements wait, every other ready node keeps executing within the request” / “then, as the kernel actor, advances every run left `running`”
open_points.question: During startup recovery, must the kernel execute all ready work in every unfinished run even when that run also has an approval or unknown-outcome wait, or does it advance only runs whose derived status is `running`?
options: Advance every ready element in every unfinished run until no element can execute
Advance only runs whose derived status is `running`
Reach only elements whose former wait was cleared, without advancing their newly ready dependants
open_points.default_guess: Advance every ready element in every unfinished run until no element can execute, preserving the independent-branch rule.

open_points.subject: draft-write effect outcome
open_points.text: “not a `draft-write` send, whose authority is the version's FlowActivation” / “The effect sent once, on the exact request the owner was shown or under the owner's grant”
open_points.question: Does the stated successful outcome also allow a `draft-write` to be sent under the run's FlowActivation without an approval preview or standing grant?
options: Yes, add FlowActivation as the third authority represented by the outcome
No, every effect in this flow must use an approval or grant
Exclude `draft-write` nodes from this reviewed flow
open_points.default_guess: Allow `draft-write` under the run's FlowActivation and treat the outcome sentence as incomplete.

open_points.subject: run-spool removal failure
open_points.text: “a store call that fails changes no record ... and the request is answered as an internal error” / “a removal that fails or is interrupted fails nothing”
open_points.question: When `capability:store.remove_run_spool` fails after a run ends or is released, does the request still succeed with cleanup deferred to startup, or return `internal_error` and stop the kernel?
options: The lifecycle change succeeds and leftover files are removed at a later start
Return `internal_error` and stop after preserving the committed lifecycle change
Roll back the run-ending or release record
open_points.default_guess: The lifecycle change and request succeed; leftover files are never served and cleanup is retried at a later start.
